text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
English monarch EDWARD III, who was defeated by ROBERT THE BRUCE at Bannockburn, was born in 1312.
Anglo-French fashion designer CHARLES FERDERICK WORTH, who was a favourite with Empress EUGENIE, was born in 1825.
English/Australian cricketer JOSEPH COATES was born in 1844. He introduced the 'yorker' to Australia and went on to become the first headmaster of Sydney Boys High School.
Scottish author ROBERT LOUIS STEVENSON, whose classics include "Treasure Island", "Kidnapped" and "The Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde", was born in 1850.
British actress ADRIENNE CORRI, who appeared in "Bunny Lake Is Missing" and "Clockwork Orange", was born in 1930.
American/Australian TV host DON LANE was born in 1933. His catchphrase was "I love your faces".
Canadian bassist with 'Glass Tiger' WAYNE PARKER was born in 1960.
** EVENTS **
1851 : A telegraphic service started between London and
Paris.
1914 : A patent was taken out on the 'bra'. The female

underwear item was known as the 'backless brassiere' which covered and supported only the breasts. It was the invention of Mrs MARY PHELPS JACOB who constructed her prototype from two hankerchiefs and baby ribbon. She had been making the bras for her friends for several years and had been persuaded to patent her idea.
1920 : The first full session of the League of Nations
began in Geneva with five thousand representatives from 41 nations.
1925 : The South African government called for more
segregation of blacks.
1939 : American HENRY JEFFERS demonstrated his invention
of the rotolactor, a rotating milking machine that could milk 1680 cows in seven hours.
1940 : Walt Disney's film "Fantasia", which depicted
various pieces of music set to cartoon and starred Leopold Stokowski and Mickey Mouse, opened in New York. It was the first film to use stereophonic sound.
1945 : General CHARLES de GAULLE was elected President of
the French provisional government.
1954 : A referendum in New South Wales favoured 10 p.m.
closing time for hotels instead of 6 p.m., which was introduced during the war.
1964 : Pope PAUL VI gave his jewelled tiara to the
world's poor.
1971 : NASA announced that "Mariner 9" was in orbit
around Mars.
1973 : A state of emergency was declared in Britain after
power workers and coal miners began industrial action.
1985 : Colombian volcano Nevado del Ruiz erupted and

completely buried the town of Armero. Few of the town's 25,000 residents survived. Warnings of the imminent eruption were ignored and there was no attempt to evacuate the area which became covered in thick ash and mud.
1986 : A Western Australian couple were charged wth
murdering four women over a three-week period. CATHERINE and DAVID BIRNIE, both 35, were apprehended after they tried to abduct a 17-year-old girl, who managed to escape and alert police.
1995 : A bomb attack on a U.S.-run military centre in
Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, killed seven people, five of them Americans.
1995 : Israel began pulling troops out of the West Bank
city of Jenin to end 28 years of occupation.
